exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Which Language to Learn
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Amy: What foreign language do you want to study, Ben?
Ben: I really want to study French. I think it sounds beautiful.
Amy: Why French? Do you want to go to France one day?
Ben: Yes, and French is used by many international organisations.
Amy: That's true. I'd like to learn Russian myself.
Ben: Russian? Why is that?
Amy: My father does business with Russians, so I can help him.
Ben: That's a great reason. Good luck with it!
exercises.translation_cn: Amy 问 Ben 想学哪门外语;Ben 想学法语,觉得好听;因为想去法国、且许多国际组织用法语;Amy 想学俄语;因为父亲和俄罗斯人做生意,她可以帮忙。

questions.stem: Which language does Ben want to study?
Why does Ben like that language?
options: It is the easiest to spell.

questions.stem: Which language does Amy want to learn?
Why does Amy want to learn it?
options: Her father does business with Russians.
Because it is required at school.

questions.stem: What is one extra reason Ben gives for his choice?
options: It is spoken only in France.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Languages of the World
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: There are about seven thousand languages in the world today.
Chinese and English have the most native speakers.
The official languages of the United Nations are spoken by billions of people.
People study a foreign language for many different reasons.
Learning one opens a door to a new way of thinking.
exercises.translation_cn: 当今世界约有七千种语言;汉语和英语母语者最多;联合国官方语言被数十亿人使用;人们学外语原因各异;学一门语言会打开通往新思维方式的大门。

questions.stem: About how many languages are there in the world?
Which two languages have the most native speakers?
Who speaks the UN's official languages?
Why do people study a foreign language?
What does learning a language open, according to the passage?
options: A window to the past only.
A door to a new way of thinking.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 A Word with Two Meanings
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Zhou Wei: I really need to buy some pants today.
Martin: Pants? That's funny. I don't usually shop for pants with friends.
Zhou Wei: You don't? Don't you want someone to tell you if they look good?
Martin: Wait, do you mean trousers, the ones we wear on our legs?
Zhou Wei: Yes! That's American English for trousers.
Martin: Ah, I see. In British English, 'pants' means underwear.
Zhou Wei: Oh! No wonder you looked surprised.
Martin: Don't worry. It's just two ways of speaking the same language.
exercises.translation_cn: 周伟说要买 pants;Martin 觉得好笑;原来周伟说的是美式英语里的'裤子';而英式英语里 pants 指内裤;两人弄懂这只是同一语言的两种说法。

questions.stem: What did Zhou Wei want to buy?
Why did Martin find it funny at first?
options: He did not like Zhou Wei.

questions.stem: In American English, what does 'pants' mean?
In British English, what does 'pants' mean?
How does Martin explain the difference?
options: It is two ways of speaking the same language.

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The Chinese Writing System
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Written Chinese began thousands of years ago as simple pictures.
Ancient people carved symbols onto animal bones and shells.
By the Shang Dynasty, these became a complete writing system.
No matter what dialect people speak, they can read the same characters.
In this way, written Chinese has helped to unite the people.
exercises.translation_cn: 汉字数千年前始于简单的图画;古人把符号刻在动物骨头和龟甲上;到商朝已成完整书写系统;不论说什么方言,人们都能读同样的字;这样汉字帮助团结了人民。

questions.stem: What did written Chinese begin as?
Where did ancient people carve the symbols?
By which dynasty had it become a complete system?
Who can read the same characters?
What has written Chinese helped to do?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Advice on Learning English
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Wang Le: I have so much trouble with my listening. Any advice?
Jia Xin: Try listening to English radio every day.
Wang Le: Does that really help?
Jia Xin: Yes. It helps you get used to how fast native speakers talk.
Wang Le: That's a good idea. What else can I do?
Jia Xin: Record your own voice and compare it with the speaker's.
Wang Le: I see. So I can hear my own mistakes.
Jia Xin: Exactly. Little by little, your listening will improve.
exercises.translation_cn: 王乐听力困难求建议;佳欣建议每天听英语广播;能帮助习惯母语者语速;还建议录下自己声音和原声比较,听出自己的错误;一点点听力就会进步。

questions.stem: What problem does Wang Le have?
What is Jia Xin's first piece of advice?
options: Listen to English radio every day.

questions.stem: How does that advice help?
options: It helps you get used to native speakers' speed.
It makes English easier to spell.

questions.stem: What is the second piece of advice?
options: Record your voice and compare it.

questions.stem: What will happen little by little?

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 A Tip for Language Learners
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone learning a new language.
Do not be afraid to make mistakes when you speak.
Every mistake is a chance to learn something new.
If you are not sure what a word means, just ask politely.
A few brave words today can open many doors tomorrow.
exercises.translation_cn: 给学新语言的人一个小贴士:说话时别怕犯错;每个错误都是学新东西的机会;不确定词义就礼貌地问;今天几句勇敢的话,明天能打开许多扇门。

questions.stem: Who is this tip for?

options: Do not be afraid of them.

questions.stem: What is every mistake, according to the passage?
options: A chance to learn something new.

questions.stem: What should you do if unsure of a word's meaning?
